candidates.statement: Manufacturers must control and assess the quality of incoming DMGs, components, containers, 333 and closures as specified in §§ 213.80, 213.82, and 213.84 because materials of poor quality can 334 adversely affect the quality and safety of the medical gas. Materials can contain impurities (e.g., 335 caused by poor air quality conditions in air separation units or inadequate purification during 336 manufacturing), or a change to the manufacturing process could affect quality (e.g., an 337 adjustment in a manufacturing step could alter the composition of a supplied gas). Any rejected 338 incoming DMGs, components, and medical gas containers and closures must be handled in 339 accordance with § 213.89, which requires rejected items to be identified and quarantined to 340 prevent their use in manufacturing or processing operations for which they are unsuitable. In 341 addition, manufacturers must document and assess the data on rejected material and take 342 appropriate corrective action (§ 213.192(a)). 343

A manufacturer 396 should reexamine a medical gas container or closure when it is exposed to adverse storage 397 conditions that could cause deterioration or contamination of the medical gas. Manufacturers 398 must also protect against container and closure leaks (§ 213.84(b)). This includes performing 399 leak tests on containers and closures and investigating any container closure defects identified 400 either during production or upon receipt of a leak complaint (§ 213.198(a)). Valve replacements 401 (e.g., due to a valve defect) should be performed as part of a planned program, with mitigation 402 strategies, and investigated as a deviation.
